title: Greece says no, 1940 — the first Axis setback of the war
sources: Wikipedia: Greco-Italian War — on the eve of 28 October 1940 Italy's ambassador Emanuele Grazzi handed Ioannis Metaxas an ultimatum from Mussolini demanding that Axis forces be allowed to occupy 'strategic positions' in Greece; Metaxas rejected it with the words 'Alors, c'est la guerre' ('Then it is war'); the popular story is that he answered 'Ochi!' ('No!'); Italian forces in Albania attacked at 05:30, half an hour before the ultimatum expired; the Italian commander Visconti Prasca had promised to finish off the Greek forces in Epirus in ten to fifteen days; on 8 November, as the failure mounted, Visconti Prasca was relieved of overall command; the Greeks then counter-attacked and pushed the Italians back into Albania; Mark Mazower called it 'the first Axis setback of the entire war'; a captured Greek officer: 'we are sure that we will lose the war, but we will give you the s[lap]...'

Wikipedia: Battle of Elaia–Kalamas (2–8 November 1940) — on 8 November the fruitless Italian offensive was suspended and the Italians began withdrawing to defensive positions; the Julia Alpine division was virtually wiped out in the Pindus
Wikipedia: Ohi Day — 28 October, commemorating the rejection of the ultimatum, is a national holiday in Greece
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1932 the Australian army withdraws from its 'war' against emus; 1520 the Stockholm Bloodbath

Photos (public domain / CC0): Greek soldier on a captured Italian tankette at Kalpaki, 1940; Greek gun crew in Albania, 1940–41 (US Office of War Information); Greek soldier holding his daughter, 1940–41 (OWI); Greek soldiers with a Hotchkiss machine gun, Albanian front 1940; the march to the Kleisoura pass; Ioannis Metaxas, 1937; Benito Mussolini; the newspaper Ellinikon Mellon, 30 October 1940 ('OXI!'); an RAF Blenheim in Greece
Illustrative stock footage (Pexels, free licence; not of the event): snowfall, a winter forest

post.facebook:
On this day in 1940, the Italian invasion of Greece ground to a halt.

In the early hours of 28 October, Italy's ambassador woke the Greek prime minister, Ioannis Metaxas, with an ultimatum from Mussolini: let Italian troops occupy Greek territory. Metaxas replied in French: "Then it is war." Greeks remember it as a single word — "Ochi". No.

Italian troops attacked from Albania half an hour before their own deadline expired. Their commander promised to finish the Greeks in two weeks. Instead, in the mountains of Epirus and the Pindus, the Greeks held, and an Italian Alpine division was nearly wiped out. On 8 November the Italian offensive was called off and its commander removed. Then the Greeks counter-attacked and pushed the Italians back into Albania.

It has been called the first Axis setback of the entire war. Greece still celebrates 28 October as Ochi Day.

Also on 8 November: Australia's army withdrew from its "Emu War" (1932), and the Stockholm Bloodbath (1520).

youtube.description:
28 October 1940: Mussolini gave Greece an ultimatum — let Italian troops occupy Greek territory. Prime minister Ioannis Metaxas replied "Then it is war"; Greeks remember it as one word, "Ochi" (No). Italy invaded from Albania promising victory in two weeks, but in the mountains the Greeks held. On 8 November 1940 the Italian offensive was called off and its commander removed; the Greeks then pushed the Italians back into Albania — the first Axis setback of the war.

Also on 8 November: the Emu War ends (1932) and the Stockholm Bloodbath (1520).
